title: Lesson 43: Are There Strangers in Space

segments.text: Lesson 43
segments.translation: 第43课

segments.text: Are there strangers in space?
segments.translation: 太空中有陌生人吗？

segments.text: Listen to the tape then answer this question.
segments.translation: 听录音，然后回答问题。

segments.text: What does the 'uniquely rational way' for us to communicate with other intelligent beings in space depend on?
segments.translation: 我们与太空中其他智慧生物交流的'独特理性方式'取决于什么？

segments.text: We must conclude from the work of those who have studied the origin of life,
segments.translation: 从研究生命起源的人的工作中，我们必须得出结论，

segments.text: that given a planet only approximately like our own, life is almost certain to start.
segments.translation: 只要有一个与我们的行星大致相似的星球，生命几乎必然会诞生。

segments.text: Of all the planets in our solar system, we are now pretty certain the Earth is the only one on which life can survive.
segments.translation: 在太阳系所有行星中，我们现在相当确定地球是唯一能维持生命的星球。

segments.text: Mars is too dry and poor in oxygen, Venus far too hot, and so is Mercury,
segments.translation: 火星太干燥且缺氧，金星太热，水星也是如此，

segments.text: and the outer planets have temperatures near absolute zero and hydrogen-dominated atmospheres.
segments.translation: 而外行星温度接近绝对零度，大气层以氢为主。

segments.text: But other suns, start as the astronomers call them, are bound to have planets like our own, and as is the number of stars in the universe is so vast,
segments.translation: 但其他恒星，正如天文学家所称呼的那样，必定拥有类似我们的行星，而且宇宙中恒星数量如此庞大，

segments.text: this possibility becomes virtual certainty.
segments.translation: 这种可能性就变成了几乎确定的事实。

segments.text: There are one hundred thousand million starts in our own Milky Way alone,
segments.translation: 仅我们银河系就有一千亿颗恒星，

segments.text: and then there are three thousand million other milky ways or galaxies, in the universe.
segments.translation: 而宇宙中还有三十亿个其他星系。

segments.text: so the number of stars that we know exist is now estimated at about 300 million million million.
segments.translation: 所以我们已知存在的恒星数量现在估计约为三万亿亿颗。

segments.text: Although perhaps only 1 percent of the life that has started somewhere will develop into highly complex and intelligent patterns,
segments.translation: 虽然在某处诞生的生命中只有1%会发展成高度复杂的智慧形态，

segments.text: so vast is the number of planets, that intelligent life is bound to be a natural part of the universe.
segments.translation: 但行星数量如此庞大，智慧生命必然是宇宙的自然组成部分。

segments.text: If then we are so certain that other intelligent life exists in the universe, why have we had no visitors from outer space yet?
segments.translation: 既然我们如此确信宇宙中存在其他智慧生命，为什么至今还没有外太空访客？

segments.text: First of all, they may have come to this planet of ours thousands or millions of years ago,
segments.translation: 首先，他们可能在数千或数百万年前就来过我们这颗行星，

segments.text: and found our then prevailing primitive state completely uninteresting to their own advanced knowledge.
segments.translation: 发现我们当时普遍的原始状态对他们先进的知识来说完全无趣。

segments.text: Professor Ronald Bracewell, a leading American radio astronomer,
segments.translation: 美国著名射电天文学家罗纳德·布雷斯韦尔教授

segments.text: argued in Nature that such a superior civilization, on a visit to our own solar system,
segments.translation: 在《自然》杂志上论证说，这样一个高级文明在访问我们太阳系时，

segments.text: may have left an automatic messenger behind to await the possible awakening of an advanced civilization.
segments.translation: 可能留下了一个自动信使来等待先进文明的觉醒。

segments.text: Such a messenger, receiving our radio and television signals,
segments.translation: 这样一个信使接收到我们的无线电和电视信号后，

segments.text: might well re-transmit them back to its home-planet,
segments.translation: 很可能会将它们转发回母星，

segments.text: although what impression any other civilization would thus get from us is best left unsaid.
segments.translation: 尽管其他文明由此对我们产生的印象最好不提。

segments.text: But here we come up against the most difficult of all obstacles to contact with people on other planets
segments.translation: 但在这里我们遇到了与其他行星上的人们联系的最大障碍

segments.text: -- the astronomical distances which separate us.
segments.translation: ——将我们分开的天文距离。

segments.text: As a reasonable guess, they might, on an average, be 100 light years away.
segments.translation: 合理猜测，它们平均可能在100光年之外。

segments.text: (A light year is the distance which light travels at 186, 000 miles per second in one year, namely 6 million million miles.)
segments.translation: （一光年是以每秒186,000英里的速度光在一年内传播的距离，即6万亿英里。）

segments.text: Radio waves also travel at the speed of light,
segments.translation: 无线电波也以光速传播，

segments.text: and assuming such an automatic messenger picked up our first broadcasts of the 1920's,
segments.translation: 假设这样一个自动信使接收到了我们1920年代的首次广播，

segments.text: the message to its home planet is barely halfway there.
segments.translation: 发送到母星的信息才走了不到一半路程。

segments.text: Similarly, our own present primitive chemical rockets,
segments.translation: 同样，我们目前原始的化学火箭，

segments.text: though good enough to orbit men, have no chance of transporting us to the nearest other star,
segments.translation: 虽然足以将人送入轨道，但没有机会将我们运送到最近的恒星，

segments.text: four light years away, let alone distances of tens or hundreds of light years.
segments.translation: 四光年之遥，更不用说几十或几百光年的距离了。

segments.text: Fortunately, there is a 'uniquely rational way' for us to communicate with other intelligent beings,
segments.translation: 幸运的是，我们有一种'独特理性的方式'与其他智慧生物交流，

segments.text: as Walter Sullivan has put it in his excellent book,
segments.translation: 正如沃尔特·沙利文在他的杰出著作中所说，

segments.text: We Are not Alone.
segments.translation: 《我们并不孤独》。

segments.text: This depends on the precise radio frequency of the 21-cm wavelength, or 1420 megacycles per second.
segments.translation: 这取决于21厘米波长的精确无线电频率，即每秒1420兆赫兹。

segments.text: It is the natural frequency of emission of the hydrogen atoms in space and was discovered by us in 1951;
segments.translation: 它是太空中氢原子辐射的自然频率，于1951年被我们发现；

segments.text: it must be known to any kind of radio astronomer in the universe.
segments.translation: 宇宙中任何射电天文学家都必定知道它。

segments.text: Once the existence of this wave-length had been discovered,
segments.translation: 一旦发现了这种波长的存在，

segments.text: it was not long before its use as the uniquely recognizable broadcasting frequency for interstellar communication was suggested.
segments.translation: 不久就有人建议将其作为星际通信唯一可识别的广播频率。

segments.text: Without something of this kind,
segments.translation: 没有这样的东西，

segments.text: searching for intelligences on other planets would be like trying to meet a friend in London without a pre-arranged rendezvous
segments.translation: 在其他行星上寻找智慧生物就像在伦敦没有事先约好地点就想见到朋友一样

segments.text: and absurdly wandering the streets in the hope of a chance encounter.
segments.translation: 荒谬地在街上游荡，希望能偶然相遇。
